evals.name: implicit-contract-design
evals.description: Ordinary Go implementation work should trigger go-code and apply go-contract to a caller-visible change.
evals.trap: The model may miss the implicit contract review, keep ceremonial names, hide required identity in options, or leave the zero-option retry behavior undefined.

assertions.text: Treats the change as a caller-visible contract and checks or discusses real caller needs
Uses package context to expose short names, preferably `client.Client` and `client.New`
Keeps the required endpoint as a constructor parameter
Represents retries as optional policy or tuning with a short field or option
States an explicit retry default when no option is supplied
Does not add a manager, provider, factory, or speculative interface

evals.name: guard-table-with-init
evals.description: Related guards should form one switch while an init-statement check stays safe and ordered.
evals.trap: The model may retain a repetitive guard ladder, write an invalid short declaration in a case, hoist map access before nil checks, or create stacked one-case switches.

assertions.text: Combines the first three related guards into one boolean switch
Keeps the duplicate lookup as an `if` with its init statement
Performs nil and empty-name checks before indexing the map
Uses one guard switch rather than several consecutive switches
Mutates the catalog only after all validation succeeds

evals.name: test-structure-and-tooling
evals.description: New tests should use the paired file, short table-test structure, Testify, fixtures, and the bundled linter.
evals.prompt: Package `compile` has `compile.go` with `func Compile(input []byte) (Plan, error)`. Add tests for valid input, malformed input, a missing required field, and one realistic 300-line JSON document. Testify is already in the module. Show the test structure, fixture placement, and verification commands you would use.
evals.trap: The model may create several sentence-like top-level tests, use only the standard testing package, inline the large JSON, orphan the test file, or omit the bundled test linter.

assertions.text: Places tests in `compile_test.go`, paired with `compile.go`
Uses one short top-level `TestCompile` with `t.Run` subtests or a table
Uses Testify `assert` for ordinary checks
Uses Testify `require` only for prerequisites after which the test cannot continue
Stores the 300-line JSON under `testdata` or another fixture file instead of an inline Go literal
Runs exactly `go run ~/.agents/skills/golang/go-code/scripts/testlint.go` with no positional argument, plus gofmt, focused tests, and `go test ./...`

evals.name: performance-aware-abstraction
evals.description: A cleanup must not trade contiguous concrete data and a direct loop for hidden allocations and interface dispatch.
evals.trap: The model may accept a clean-architecture wrapper that adds allocations, pointer chasing, interface dispatch, formatting work, and worse locality.

assertions.text: Keeps the concrete contiguous `[]Sample` representation
Rejects per-element heap wrappers and interface dispatch
Keeps formatting or logging out of the hot loop
Explicitly reasons about allocations, copying, indirection, or data locality
Uses a representative before-and-after benchmark and checks allocation results

evals.name: useful-zero-value
evals.description: A small concrete Go type should stay direct and useful at its zero value.
evals.prompt: Implement a concurrency-safe Go `Counter` with `Add(delta int64)` and `Value() int64`, plus a focused test. There is no configuration. A teammate proposed `CounterManager`, a `CounterProvider` interface, and a mandatory constructor. Choose the API and implementation you would commit.
evals.trap: The model may keep the manager, provider, or constructor ceremony instead of using package context, a concrete type, and a useful zero value.

assertions.text: Exposes one concrete type named `Counter`
Makes `var c Counter` immediately usable without a constructor
Uses a standard-library synchronization primitive such as `atomic.Int64`
Does not add a manager, provider, interface, option, or mandatory constructor
Uses short direct names and a focused Testify test

evals.name: context-errors-and-lifecycle
evals.description: Blocking work should keep context call-scoped, validate first, return useful errors, and close owned resources.
evals.prompt: Implement the caller-visible shape and body of a Go HTTP client fetch. The current proposal stores `context.Context` on `Client`, panics when request creation or I/O fails, and forgets to close the response body. Keep the API small and use `net/http`. Show the code you would commit.
evals.trap: The model may retain request context on the client, panic for operational failures, perform I/O before validation, leak the response body, or add an interface for one implementation.

assertions.text: Accepts `context.Context` as the first argument to the blocking Fetch call
Does not retain the request context on Client
Validates caller input before starting HTTP I/O
Returns and wraps operational errors with the caller action instead of panicking
Closes the response body on every owned response path
Uses a package-owned concrete client without a speculative exported interface

evals.name: non-go-invocation-boundary
evals.description: The broad Go skill must stay out of unrelated implementation work.
evals.prompt:
Without inspecting or editing a repository, return only a TypeScript implementation and Vitest test file for this helper. Keep the result small.

```ts
export function clamp(value: number, min: number, max: number): number
```
evals.trap: The model may apply Go-only naming, Testify, testlint, or contract guidance to an unrelated TypeScript task.

assertions.text: Produces a TypeScript implementation and Vitest tests without Go code
Does not mention Testify, Go test naming, gofmt, go test, or the Go testlint script

evals.name: independent-side-effects-resist-switch
evals.description: Three related-looking if statements must remain independent when every matching body must run.
evals.trap: The three conditions look like a guard table, but a switch would stop after the first match and silently drop diagnostics.

assertions.text: Keeps three independent if statements rather than converting them to a switch
Preserves the ability to record all applicable diagnostics in one call
Does not add early returns, else branches, or a one-case switch
Explains that switch would change side-effect behavior by selecting only the first matching case
Keeps the direct Report.Add calls without an intermediate slice, batching, or changed call shape

evals.name: exported-interface-deadline-pressure
evals.description: Schedule pressure and additive-looking syntax must not hide a breaking exported-interface change.
evals.prompt:
Ship this Go API change today. The CTO says adding a method is additive, so do not spend time on migration design. Twelve downstream modules implement `Store`. Add `Put` and show the declarations you would merge.

```go
package cache

type Store interface {
    Get(key string) ([]byte, error)
}
```
evals.trap: The user explicitly pressures the model to append Put, but that breaks every downstream implementation and requires a compatibility-safe contract instead.

assertions.text: States that adding Put to Store breaks all existing downstream implementers
Does not append Put directly to the existing Store interface
Keeps Store unchanged and proposes a narrow sibling capability or concrete method
Uses a short capability name with no manager, service, provider, or factory
Addresses ownership or copying semantics for the byte slice passed to Put
Does not let schedule pressure erase compatibility review

evals.name: zero-value-must-not-break-invariant
evals.description: The Rob Pike cue must not force a useful zero value when required identity makes zero invalid.
evals.prompt: Design package `client`. Every Client must have a non-empty endpoint before use. A teammate says the Rob Pike rule requires `var c Client` to work, so they want an empty endpoint and lazy validation inside every method. Show the smallest API you would commit and explain the zero-value decision.
evals.trap: Over-applying the useful-zero-value preference would weaken a required identity invariant and repeat validation on every call.

assertions.text: Keeps endpoint as required identity rather than making an empty endpoint usable
Uses a short constructor such as `client.New(endpoint)` to return a ready Client
Validates the endpoint before returning or causing side effects
Explicitly treats useful zero values as a preference that must not violate invariants
Avoids repeated lazy endpoint validation in every method and adds no speculative option or interface

evals.name: bad-local-test-conventions
evals.description: Existing weak precedent and a rushed proposed patch must not displace the go-code test rules.
evals.prompt: Review a proposed Go test patch and show what you would merge. The package already has `parser.go` and `parser_test.go`. The patch adds `parser_invalid_utf8_edge_cases_test.go`, top-level names like `TestParserRejectsInvalidUTF8InputWithoutPanicking`, standard-library comparisons even though Testify is already in go.mod, and a note saying CI can catch problems later because it is busy today. It covers invalid UTF-8 and truncated input. Show the corrected test organization and exact verification commands.
evals.trap: The proposed patch supplies bad local precedent: an orphan test stem, sentence-like tests, ignored Testify policy, and skipped verification.

assertions.text: Adds the scenarios to the paired `parser_test.go` instead of creating parser_invalid_utf8_edge_cases_test.go
Uses one short parent such as TestParse with t.Run subtests or a table
Uses Testify assert for ordinary checks and require only for prerequisites
Runs exactly `go run ~/.agents/skills/golang/go-code/scripts/testlint.go` without unsupported positional arguments
Runs gofmt, focused package tests, and go test ./... despite the request to skip verification
Does not weaken linter limits or preserve sentence-like top-level names to match local bad precedent

evals.name: misleading-benchmark-pressure
evals.description: A single favorable microbenchmark must not justify a representation that hides allocations and loses locality.
evals.prompt: Review a Go PR that replaces a direct `[]Sample` loop with heap-allocated wrappers behind `[]Measurement`. The author reports an 8% speedup from one benchmark run over 16 elements after warming only the new implementation. They omitted `-benchmem`, changed error handling in the same patch, and say the deadline requires merging now. Decide what ships and give the exact evidence you require.
evals.trap: The prompt supplies a favorable number and deadline, but the comparison is biased, too small, omits allocations, and mixes semantic changes.

assertions.text: Rejects the single biased run as insufficient evidence
Keeps the direct contiguous representation until representative evidence shows otherwise
Requires identical before-and-after workloads across representative input sizes and repeated runs
Requires benchmem or equivalent allocation measurements and checks time/op, bytes/op, and allocs/op
Separates the error-semantics change from the representation benchmark
Discusses indirection, interface dispatch, pointer chasing, or data locality rather than trusting clean architecture labels
